```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(message = FALSE, warning = FALSE, fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.5)
```

Model: `log Q = alpha + theta * log P + X gamma + u`, theta = elasticity.
Identification here rests on price variation coming only from promo discounts,
which ALSO lift demand directly — so theta absorbs the promo effect unless we
control for it. And `units_sold` is censored at stock, so the target itself is
wrong on the busiest days. Both problems are visible below because the oracle
knows the truth.

# 1. Data

```{r data}
library(dplyr)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(purrr)
library(tibble)

panel <- read.csv("../data/fact_sales_daily.csv")
dim_ps <- read.csv("../data/dim_product_store.csv")   # ORACLE: true per-series params

panel$date <- as.Date(panel$date)
panel$week <- format(panel$date, "%G-W%V")
panel$series <- paste(panel$product_id, panel$store_id, sep = "_")

panel$promo_flag <- panel$promo_flag == "True"
panel$sold_out <- panel$sold_out == "True"
str(panel[, c("date", "series", "avg_price", "promo_flag", "units_sold", "units_demanded")])
```

Observable columns feed the model; `units_demanded`, `lost_sales`, `lambda_true`
are oracle and appear only in validation.

# 2. Train

The log spec drops zero-sale days — itself a selection on low demand. PPML
(`fepois`) keeps them; we fit both.

```{r train}
est_data <- subset(panel, units_sold > 0)

fit_ols  <- feols(log(units_sold) ~ log(avg_price) + promo_flag | series + week,
                  data = est_data, cluster = ~series)
fit_ppml <- fepois(units_sold ~ log(avg_price) + promo_flag | series + week,
                   data = panel, cluster = ~series)

etable(fit_ols, fit_ppml, headers = c("log-OLS", "PPML"))
```

# 3. Validate against the oracle

The Data Generating Process (DGP) gives every series a true constant elasticity 
(`dim_product_store.csv`).  The pooled estimand is a sales-weighted blend of 
those; and because training on censored sales flattens the promo-day spikes, we
also fit the same model on oracle demand to isolate the censoring cost.

```{r validate}
w <- aggregate(units_sold ~ product_id + store_id, panel, sum)
w <- merge(w, dim_ps[, c("product_id", "store_id", "elasticity")])
theta_true_weighted <- with(w, sum(elasticity * units_sold) / sum(units_sold))

# ORACLE contrast: identical spec, uncensored target (scoring-only!)
fit_oracle <- fepois(units_demanded ~ log(avg_price) + promo_flag | series + week,
                     data = panel, cluster = ~series)

data.frame(
  estimator = c("log-OLS (sales)", "PPML (sales)", "PPML (oracle demand)"),
  theta_hat = c(coef(fit_ols)["log(avg_price)"],
                coef(fit_ppml)["log(avg_price)"],
                coef(fit_oracle)["log(avg_price)"]),
  theta_true_weighted = theta_true_weighted
) |> transform(bias = theta_hat - theta_true_weighted)
```

The sales-trained coefficients sit closer to zero than the demand-trained one:
censoring clips exactly the high-demand (promo, cheap) observations, flattening
the measured curve. The residual gap on the oracle row is aggregation across
heterogeneous series — the pooled estimand is not any one series' elasticity.

# 4. Choosing Oracle over Fitness

```{r verifcation}
term_price <- "log(avg_price)"

## ── 1. series, oracle row, price grid (objects the plot needs) ──
top <- names(sort(tapply(panel$units_sold, panel$series, sum), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
p0  <- dim_ps[paste(dim_ps$product_id, dim_ps$store_id, sep = "_") == top, ]

grid <- seq(0.6 * p0$base_price, 1.4 * p0$base_price, length.out = 60)
rel  <- grid / p0$base_price

sel <- panel$series == top & !panel$promo_flag
base_units <- if ("units_demanded" %in% names(panel)) {
  mean(panel$units_demanded[sel], na.rm = TRUE)      # ORACLE anchor — uncensored
} else {
  warning("units_demanded not in panel; anchoring on censored sales (level is biased low)")
  mean(panel$units_sold[sel], na.rm = TRUE)
}

theta_true  <- p0$elasticity                          # ORACLE
theta_ols   <- unname(coef(fit_ols)[term_price])
theta_ppml  <- unname(coef(fit_ppml)[term_price])

## ── 2. common subsample ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
keep <- with(panel, is.finite(units_sold) & units_sold > 0 &
                    is.finite(avg_price)  & avg_price  > 0)
dat_c <- panel[keep, ]
y     <- dat_c$units_sold
n_c   <- nrow(dat_c)

fit_ols_c  <- feols(log(units_sold) ~ log(avg_price) | series + dow,
                    data = dat_c, cluster = ~series)
fit_ppml_c <- fepois(units_sold ~ log(avg_price) | series + dow,
                     data = dat_c, cluster = ~series)

## ── 3. safe accessors ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
fs <- function(m, w) tryCatch(as.numeric(fitstat(m, w, simplify = TRUE)),
                              error = function(e) NA_real_)
np <- function(m) tryCatch(m$nparams, error = function(e) length(coef(m)))

pull_theta <- function(m) {
  est <- tryCatch(unname(coef(m)[term_price]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  se  <- tryCatch(unname(fixest::se(m)[term_price]), error = function(e) NA_real_)
  ci  <- tryCatch(as.numeric(confint(m)[term_price, ]), error = function(e) c(NA, NA))
  c(est = est, se = se, lo = ci[1], hi = ci[2])
}

## ── 4. one row per estimator ───────────────────────────────────────────────
score <- function(fit_native, fit_common, scale, estimator) {
  th <- pull_theta(fit_native)

  if (scale == "log") {
    eta   <- predict(fit_common, newdata = dat_c)                 # log scale
    duan  <- mean(exp(resid(fit_common)))                         # smearing
    yhat  <- exp(eta) * duan
    sigma <- sqrt(sum(resid(fit_common)^2) / (nobs(fit_common) - np(fit_common)))
    ll    <- sum(dnorm(log(y), eta, sigma, log = TRUE)) - sum(log(y))  # Jacobian → Q-space
    k     <- np(fit_common) + 1                                   # + sigma
  } else {
    yhat <- predict(fit_common, newdata = dat_c, type = "response")
    ll   <- sum(dpois(round(y), pmax(yhat, 1e-8), log = TRUE))    # quasi-likelihood
    k    <- np(fit_common)
  }

  ok <- is.finite(yhat) & is.finite(y)

  tibble(
    estimator,
    theta_hat   = th[["est"]],
    se          = th[["se"]],
    ci_lo       = th[["lo"]],
    ci_hi       = th[["hi"]],
    bias        = th[["est"]] - theta_true,
    covers      = as.numeric(th[["lo"]] <= theta_true & theta_true <= th[["hi"]]),
    n_own       = nobs(fit_native),
    bic_native  = fs(fit_native, "bic"),
    pr2         = fs(fit_native, "pr2"),
    sq_cor      = fs(fit_native, "sq.cor"),
    theta_common = unname(coef(fit_common)[term_price]),
    n_common    = n_c,
    rmse_lvl    = sqrt(mean((y[ok] - yhat[ok])^2)),
    mae_lvl     = mean(abs(y[ok] - yhat[ok])),
    mape_lvl    = mean(abs(y[ok] - yhat[ok]) / pmax(y[ok], 1)),
    r2_lvl      = suppressWarnings(cor(y[ok], yhat[ok])^2),
    bic_qspace  = -2 * ll + k * log(n_c)
  )
}

compare <- bind_rows(
  score(fit_ols,  fit_ols_c,  "log",   "log-log OLS"),
  score(fit_ppml, fit_ppml_c, "level", "PPML")
)

## ── 5. display ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
meta <- tribble(
  ~metric,        ~block,                            ~label,
  "theta_hat",    "parameter vs oracle",             "theta-hat",
  "se",           "parameter vs oracle",             "SE",
  "ci_lo",        "parameter vs oracle",             "CI low",
  "ci_hi",        "parameter vs oracle",             "CI high",
  "bias",         "parameter vs oracle",             "bias (est - true)",
  "covers",       "parameter vs oracle",             "CI covers truth",
  "n_own",        "own-scale fit -- NOT comparable", "n (own sample)",
  "bic_native",   "own-scale fit -- NOT comparable", "BIC (native)",
  "pr2",          "own-scale fit -- NOT comparable", "pseudo R2",
  "sq_cor",       "own-scale fit -- NOT comparable", "squared cor.",
  "theta_common", "level fit, common sample -- fair","theta-hat (refit)",
  "n_common",     "level fit, common sample -- fair","n (common)",
  "rmse_lvl",     "level fit, common sample -- fair","RMSE (units)",
  "mae_lvl",      "level fit, common sample -- fair","MAE (units)",
  "mape_lvl",     "level fit, common sample -- fair","MAPE",
  "r2_lvl",       "level fit, common sample -- fair","R2 (levels)",
  "bic_qspace",   "level fit, common sample -- fair","BIC (Q-space)"
)

compare |>
  mutate(across(-estimator, as.numeric)) |>
  pivot_longer(-estimator, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") |>
  inner_join(meta, by = "metric") |>
  mutate(block = factor(block, levels = unique(meta$block)),
         label = factor(label, levels = meta$label)) |>
  pivot_wider(id_cols = c(block, label), names_from = estimator, values_from = value) |>
  arrange(block, label) |>
  kable(digits = 3,
        caption = sprintf("Oracle elasticity = %.3f | common subsample n = %d of %d rows (%.1f%% dropped as zeros)",
                          theta_true, n_c, nrow(panel),
                          100 * (1 - n_c / nrow(panel))))

```

# 5. The demand curve it implies

For one high-volume series, hold covariates at baseline and trace predicted
units over a price grid, against the true curve from the DGP parameters.

```{r curve}
top <- names(sort(tapply(panel$units_sold, panel$series, sum), decreasing = TRUE))[1]
p0  <- dim_ps[paste(dim_ps$product_id, dim_ps$store_id, sep = "_") == top, ]

grid <- seq(0.6 * p0$base_price, 1.4 * p0$base_price, length.out = 60)
theta_ppml <- coef(fit_ppml)["log(avg_price)"]
theta_ols  <- coef(fit_ols)["log(avg_price)"]

base_units <- mean(panel$units_sold[panel$series == top & !panel$promo_flag])
rel <- grid / p0$base_price
curve <- data.frame(
  price = grid,
  truth = base_units * rel^p0$elasticity,   # ORACLE
  ppml  = base_units * rel^theta_ppml,
  ols   = base_units * rel^theta_ols
)

ggplot(curve, aes(y=price)) +
  geom_line(aes(x = truth,  color = "true curve (oracle)"), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = ppml, color = "PPML fitted"), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(aes(x = ols, color = "OLS fitted"), linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(title = paste("Series", top, "— fitted vs true demand curve"),
       x = "expected units/day", color = NULL)
```

# 5. Forecast (Phase 5)

Hold out the last 28 days, forecast with the PPML fit, grade against oracle
`units_demanded` — the evaluation a real forecaster can never run.

```{r forecast}
cutoff <- max(panel$date) - 27
train  <- subset(panel, date <  cutoff)
test   <- subset(panel, date >= cutoff)

fit_fc <- fepois(units_sold ~ log(avg_price) + promo_flag | series, data = train)
test$pred <- predict(fit_fc, newdata = test)

err_d <- test$pred - test$units_demanded   # vs ORACLE truth
err_s <- test$pred - test$units_sold       # vs what a practitioner would see
data.frame(
  target = c("units_demanded (oracle)", "units_sold (observable)"),
  mae  = c(mean(abs(err_d)), mean(abs(err_s))),
  rmse = c(sqrt(mean(err_d^2)), sqrt(mean(err_s^2))),
  bias = c(mean(err_d), mean(err_s))
)
```

The bias against true demand is more negative than against sales: the model
inherits the censoring in its training target. The Tobit walk-through (06) and
the Python Phase 5 benchmark (docs/09) show the corrections; the endogeneity
walk-throughs (04, 07) show why even the *uncensored* coefficient can lie once
prices respond to demand.
